HUNTING STUDIES, 2026-11-20
Three ways to act on a big move, measured on 45 sessions of the whole US market. Costs taken off. Doing nothing scores 0%.

1. FLAG STUDY
A jump of 20%+ on at least 5x normal volume, then 3+ quiet days on drying volume, then a break above the quiet range. Bought on the break, stop at the bottom of the range, out after 5 sessions.

CONCLUSION: The flag has too few trades on stocks of 5 USD and over to judge (14). Watch only.

What became of 263 heavy-volume jumps: 223 never formed a flag, 16 formed one and broke down, 7 went nowhere, 0 gapped away with no fair entry, 17 broke out and gave an entry.
All flag trades: average -4.8%, typical -1.3%, 13% ended higher (16 trades)
5 USD and over: average -4.1%, typical -1.1%, 14% ended higher (14 trades)
Under 5 USD: average -10.3%, typical -4.7%, 0% ended higher (2 trades)
Compare, buying the morning after the jump: typical -5.1%, 38% ended higher (823 cases).

2. FLAG PULLBACK (after the break, wait for a return to the break level that holds)
5 USD and over: average -4.1%, typical -0.9%, 29% ended higher (7 trades)

3. EXPANSION DAY (up 1.5x its normal daily range or more on 2x volume or more; bought at the next open; stop 1x that range, target 3x, out after 10 sessions)
5 USD and over: average -0.2%, typical -2.1%, 28% ended higher (838 trades). Of these, 22% reached the target, 70% hit the stop, 7% ran out of time.
Under 5 USD: average -3.0%, typical -5.8%, 18% ended higher (80 trades)
CONCLUSION: the expansion day did NOT make money in this sample. Do not trade it.
A target three times the stop is reached far less often than the stop. The numbers above are what that trade-off really paid.

IN A FLAG NOW (3), watch only
